:::{#def-empirical-distribution}
#### Empirical distribution

For observed values $\dsn{x}$,
the **empirical distribution** is the distribution of a value
[chosen at random](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-random-choice)
from the sample, each of the $n$ observations being equally likely:
the probability that the value falls in a set $A$ is

$$\frac{1}{n}\sumjn \indicp{x_j \in A}.$$

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

#### What "empirical" means

"Empirical" means computed from the observed data,
not from a model or a population.
An empirical quantity is the matching population quantity
with the [population distribution](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-population-distribution)
replaced by the empirical distribution.
For example, the mean of the empirical distribution is the
[sample mean](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-mean),
and its CDF is the [empirical CDF](#def-empirical-cdf).
Machine learning uses the same replacement
to turn the risk of a prediction model into its *empirical risk*.

Because it needs only the data in hand, an empirical quantity can always be computed,
and it serves as an estimate of the population quantity it mimics.
@efron1993introduction build the bootstrap on this replacement.

:::
